newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to merge air/sea search and rescue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to merge air/sea search and rescue.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Wednesday the government would establish a national centre for the co-ordination of civil search and rescue operations.
Under the plan, the functions of Air Services Australia and the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) would be merged and rescue operations would be co-ordinated from Canberra.

"This will improve the communication, the effectiveness and the likelihood of survival of people who are lost at sea or indeed, lost anywhere in the country and who need rescuing," Sharp told reporters.
"We think this will lead to a quicker response and a more effective outcome and a higher rate of survival for those people who are lost and in need of help."
Sharp said it was estimated that a merger of the operations would cost about A$5.0 million for relocations and re-training.
"This is not being done for the purpose of saving money -- it's being done to save lives," he said.
The AMSA was involved in last week's successful rescue of round-the-world yachtsman, Briton Tony Bullimore and Frenchman Thierry Dubois, whose boats had capsized southwest of Australia.
It also helped to co-ordinate the rescue of fellow competitor, Frenchman Raphael Dinelli, from his sinking yacht south of Australia the day after Christmas.
